title: RAG4GFM: Bridging Knowledge Gaps in Graph Foundation Models through Graph

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Abstract claims 'achieving near-perfect accuracy in all tested scenarios' but the reported results (e.g., highest classification accuracy ≈87%, link prediction accuracy ≈60%, graph classification accuracy ≈68%) are far from near-perfect.
Text states: 'GLEM+RAG4GFM achieves 83.12% accuracy on node classification in the Computers dataset'. Table 2 shows GLEM+RAG4GFM accuracy on Computers is 87.34%. The numbers do not match.

Text claims GraphGPT+RAG4GFM outperforms its vanilla counterpart by 5.1% on link prediction (60.37% vs 54.27%). The actual difference in Table 2 is 6.1 percentage points. The stated gain is incorrect.
Table 2 contains columns for a 'Fitness' dataset, but Table 1 and Section 4.1 list only Books-Children, Books-History, Ele-Computers, and Ele-Photo. 'Fitness' is not introduced anywhere.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.3, topological structure enhancement (Eq. 10) and surrounding text
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The topological fusion adds adjacency matrices A_i of retrieved graphs to the query graph's adjacency A, but no mechanism is described to align nodes between the query graph and the retrieved graphs. Without alignment, the operation is undefined and the method cannot work as described.

predicted_errors.error_location: Sections 3.2-3.3, feature fusion for edge tasks
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: For edge-level tasks, the task-aware retriever retrieves edge features h_e (Eq. 4). However, the fusion module (Eqs. 5-9) only uses node features from the retrieved graphs and does not incorporate the retrieved edge features, making that part of the retrieval irrelevant to the augmentation.
Abstract claims 'constant-time retrieval and fusion', while Section 3.1 states 'O(log_2 N) end-to-end retrieval and fusion time'. Constant time and logarithmic time are contradictory.

The claim of 'O(log N) end-to-end retrieval and fusion time' is false because the fusion step (attention-based aggregation and adjacency operations) costs O(k|E|) or O(k|V|^2), not logarithmic. The total complexity is not O(log N) in general.

Table 3 compares RAG4GFM (AnyGraph-based) with prompt-engineering and OOD methods, but the base GFM used for Few-shot Learning, CoT, Prototype, etc. is not specified. Without this information the comparisons are not reproducible and may be unfair.
